Panel 1, THE CHASE BEGINS: front tracking medium close-up, handheld, in THE ALLEY at dusk. THE WOMAN sprints straight toward the camera, a pistol in each hand, mouth open breathing hard, glancing back over her shoulder. Far behind her, a horde of THE ZOMBIES floods round the corner into the alley. Panel 2, THE VAULT: low camera close behind THE WOMAN, following her. She vaults over the hood of the burnt-out car, body horizontal in the air. Sprinting zombies blur past both edges of the frame close to the camera, closing in. Panel 3, THE SPIN SHOT: camera behind her. Still running forward, she has spun her upper body back toward the camera and fires both pistols backward, bright orange muzzle flashes; the two lead zombies a few metres behind her stumble and fall. Panel 4, THE WALL JUMP, slow motion: side view, camera level with her. THE WOMAN moves from the left of the frame to the right. She has run up the brick alley wall and kicks off it, her body high in the air and nearly horizontal, hair streaming; below her a zombie lunges out of a broken side doorway, arms reaching up, missing her; she fires one pistol down at it, a muzzle flash. Dust hangs frozen in the air. Panel 5, THE LANDING: camera behind her, low. She lands in a forward roll on the cracked asphalt and is already coming up into a sprint away from the camera, deeper into the alley. Panel 6, THE SLAB: low angle looking up. THE WOMAN sprints up the collapsed concrete slab that leans from the broken wall to the low rooftop, silhouetted against the orange dusk sky; below her, zombies scramble and climb up the slab on hands and feet. Panel 7, THE ROOFTOPS: wide shot, camera behind her. She sprints across a flat tar rooftop toward its edge; ahead, more flat rooftops with water towers and antennas under the orange dusk sky; behind her, a horde of zombies pours over the roof edge after her. Panel 8, THE GAP JUMP, slow motion: wide side view at roof height. THE WOMAN moves from the left of the frame to the right. She is in mid-air over the deep narrow gap between two buildings, the alley far below, legs stretched in a long leap, twisted at the waist, firing both pistols back over her shoulder, orange muzzle flashes. Behind her two zombies have leapt from the far edge and are falling short into the gap. The low sun behind her, ash in the air. Panel 9, THE LAST ONE: low front angle on the far rooftop. THE WOMAN kneels where she landed, both pistols raised straight at the camera side; one zombie has made the jump and lunges at her from the near roof edge; across the gap behind her, the horde piles up at the far edge. THE ZOMBIES are fast modern runner zombies: grey mottled skin, clouded eyes, torn dirty everyday clothes, mouths open, sprinting and climbing with wild energy. Gritty and frightening but not gory: no blood, no wounds, no gore. THE WOMAN is identical in every panel that holds her, exactly as on her reference sheet: black hair with a violet sheen in a tight low ponytail, violet eyes, freckles, dark lips, the dark rune tattoo on HER RIGHT cheekbone only (the left side of the picture when she faces the camera), patched dark-brown leather jacket over a charcoal hoodie, black chest rig with magazine pouches, torn olive cargo pants, duct-taped boots, fingerless gloves, a holster on each thigh, two black pistols. She is the only living person. THE ALLEY and the rooftops are the ruined city of the environment reference, at dusk: amber-orange sky through ash haze, the alley in cold blue shadow, warm rim light on edges, drifting ash. One identical style for all nine panels: photoreal live-action cinematography on a cinema camera, real skin with pores, real materials, physically accurate light, motion blur on fast action, fine film grain. No text, no numbers, no letters anywhere.
